title: Power Apps: modernised Personal settings experience in model-driven apps

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: the briefing presents the general New Look setting as a control for the personal settings redesign without documentation confirming that connection. It also labels licensing as included and rules out direct costs without supporting Microsoft text; the roadmap facts and documented user navigation otherwise check out.

claims.claim: Licensing for the modern Personal settings experience is included in an existing product licence.
claims.quote: Searched: '"modern" "Personal settings" "license" Power Apps'; 'Power Apps modern Personal settings pricing licensing consumption'. Read set-personal-options, modern-fluent-design and appearance-settings; licensing search excerpts give no feature-specific inclusion statement.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to "unknown" and notes to "Feature-specific licensing has not been published." Neither the roadmap nor the cited Learn pages states inclusion or names a qualifying existing licence.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row

claims.fix: If retaining this historical setting, include the omitted solution selection: Solutions > solution > Add existing > More > Setting > New look for model driven apps. Explain that this opens the add-setting selector, not the value editor; do not present it as a current panel switch.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: No API or automation surface is documented for the New Look app setting.
claims.quote:
saveSettingValue
Adds or updates the setting app value for the current app or the setting environment value for the current environment.
claims.fix: Remove the obsolete New Look control row from this briefing. If describing solution-setting automation elsewhere, cite this reference and its SaveSettingValue Web API link; distinguish the documented generic setting API from whether the now-ignored New Look value has any effect.

claims.where: controls[0]; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The New Look app setting is a governance control for the modern Personal settings panel.
claims.quote: Searched: '"modern" "personal settings" "enable" "admin" Power Apps'; '"New look for model driven apps" "API"'. Read set-personal-options, modern-fluent-design and app-properties. None identifies this setting as governing the Personal settings panel.
claims.fix: Remove this row or explicitly label it general historical context with no confirmed applicability to Personal settings. The cited modern-fluent-design page says New Look became mandatory in April 2026; app-properties says its setting is hidden and ignored with 2026 Wave 1. Do not equate it with Switch to classic inside Personal settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No new data access is described for this Personal settings redesign.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Personal settings" "modern" "unchanged" "data"'. Read the roadmap, set-personal-options and appearance-settings; no new data-access permission or boundary is described for the panel redesign.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls: closing prose; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The personal options and their behaviour are unchanged from the classic experience.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Personal settings" "modern" "unchanged" "data"'. Read set-personal-options, appearance-settings and modern-fluent-design. They describe current options but do not state complete behavioural parity with the classic dialog.
claims.fix: Remove the categorical parity statements, including "behaviour is unchanged" in the rationale. Say instead: "Microsoft documents time zone, currency, email tracking and synchronisation options in Personal settings."

claims.claim: Users can set their privacy preference, subject to the organisation override described later in the briefing.
claims.quote: Specify what you want Dynamics 365 to do when an error occurs. Based on your selection, the error reports are shared with and used by Microsoft for product improvements.

claims.claim: Users can set whether other users may send email on their behalf.
claims.quote: Allow other users to send email on your behalf. | Select this option to allow other users of Dynamics 365 to send email on your behalf.

claims.claim: No autonomous behaviour is involved.
claims.quote: Searched: '"personal settings" "modern" "autonomous"'. Read set-personal-options and appearance-settings. They describe user-driven preferences, but no passage expressly states the claimed absence of autonomous behaviour.
claims.fix: Replace the categorical statement with the narrower evidence-based wording: "No autonomous capability is described in the roadmap or the Personal settings documentation."

claims.claim: The redesign's cost is limited to communications, documentation updates and support time.
claims.quote: Searched: '"modernized Personal settings" "license" "cost"'; 'Power Apps modern Personal settings pricing licensing consumption'. Read the roadmap and cited Learn pages; none expressly rules out direct licensing or consumption costs for this feature.
claims.fix: Replace with "Plan for communications, documentation updates and support time. Feature-specific licensing and consumption details have not been published." Retain cost: low as an estimate of known indirect work, not a guarantee of no direct cost.

claims.claim: No consumption change or further feature-specific charging detail is published.
claims.quote: Searched: '"modernized Personal settings" "license" "cost"'; 'Power Apps modern Personal settings pricing licensing consumption'. Read the roadmap, set-personal-options, modern-fluent-design and appearance-settings; no redesign-specific meter or consumption change found.

claims.claim: The modern Personal settings panel ships with the modern look.
claims.quote: Searched: '"modern" "personal settings" "enable" "admin" Power Apps'; 'Power Apps "NewLook" "setting" API'. Read set-personal-options, modern-fluent-design and app-properties. None states that this panel ships as part of the New Look modernization wave.
claims.fix: Remove "The panel ships with the modern look". State the independently documented fact instead: "Microsoft Learn describes modern Personal settings as the default for model-driven apps."

claims.claim: An organisation-wide privacy preference in System Settings can hide the Personal settings Privacy tab.
claims.quote: This tab isn't available if your system administrator selects the privacy preference for the entire organization in System Settings.

claims.claim: The linked appearance settings documentation describes display density defaults.
claims.quote: The default value for the Display density setting is Comfortable.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a date for removing the classic Personal settings experience.
claims.quote: Searched: '"personal settings" "classic" "removed" "date" Power Apps'. Read set-personal-options and returned deprecation excerpts; the Personal settings page says only "a future release" and no removal date was found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether admins can hide the Personal settings Switch to classic button.
claims.quote: Searched: '"personal settings" "modern" "hide" "classic" Power Apps'; '"Personal settings" "Switch to classic" admin disable setting'. Read set-personal-options and settings-behavior excerpts; the latter's classic switch concerns makers' designers, not this panel.

claims.claim: The review action rating fits an on-by-default redesign that the briefing says needs rollout communications.
claims.quote: action: "review"; "The feature scope is users, enabled by default."; "Tell users where Personal settings sits and that Switch to classic is a temporary route."
claims.fix: Set action to "prepare". The assessment scale assigns prepare to an automatic redesign needing communication; review is for an optional capability or control that changes nothing until an admin or maker chooses it.
